Closed-die hammer forging

Near-net hammer forgings

Billets heated by induction, forged in closed dies under a belt drop hammer, then trimmed on power presses. Grain flow follows the shape of the part.

From bar to dispatch

Every part starts as tested steel.

Quality is built into each step of the route, not added at the end. "The next inspector is the customer."

  • Approved steel millsBar from ISMT, JSW, Gerdau, Bhushan and VSP.
  • Colour-coded bar endsEvery bar is marked with its grade on both ends.
  • Spectro-checkedChemistry verified on a GNR spectrometer before cutting.
  • One-heat formingUpset, pierced and rolled in a single heat.
  • Logged annealingBell furnaces record every cycle on I-TOOL software.
  • Checked before dispatchHardness, visual and MPI on critical parts. Inspection report with every lot.
Shop-floor capacity

Built for 0.1 to 20 kg forgings.

Two plants, three forging routes and in-house heat treatment. One supplier from bar to machined part.

1.5 MTBelt drop hammer

3 × 3 MTBell annealing furnaces

In-house laboratory

Tested, logged, traceable.

Real photos from our laboratory and inspection area.

01 · CHEMISTRY

Spectrometer

GNR optical emission spectrometer with nitrogen detection, for incoming bar and production checks.

02 · HARDNESS

Brinell testing

3000 kg load, 10 mm ball, after heat treatment. Microstructure checked to 1000×.

03 · CRACK DETECTION

Magnetic particle

Wet MPI up to 400 mm with auto demagnetising, for functionally critical parts on request.

04 · DISPATCH

Pre-dispatch report

Dimensional and visual inspection, with a PDI report sent with every lot.

About us

Two plants. One team.

Vimal Steel Forge began ring rolling at Shapar in 2009. Vimal Forge LLP added a larger forging, heat-treatment and machining plant at Pipadiya, near Gondal.
